title: Load a tube furnace for MoS2 growth by thermal CVD
instruction: Load the three boats into the tube for MoS2 growth by thermal CVD, in the right places for the gas flow and the heat, then put the push rod back on its rests.
context: Placing precursors along a furnace's temperature profile is the step that decides whether MoS2 grows; it takes knowing the chemistry and pushing boats blind along a tube with a rod.
setup: A split-tube furnace, 410 x 280 mm, lid open, on the bench: heated length between its end walls 410 mm, a thermocouple tip at the chamber's centre. In it a fixed fused-quartz tube, 50.8 mm OD, 46 mm ID, 610 mm long, both end caps off and hung beside its ends: the argon inlet's cap at the near (right hand) end, the exhaust's cap at the far end. Beside the near end, a stainless tray holds three loose boats side by side, each with a 6 mm round tongue at its back: an alumina boat 60 x 20 x 12 mm with 4 mm of yellow sulfur powder, 12 g; an alumina boat 60 x 20 x 12 mm with 4 mm of pale MoO3 powder, 12 g; a quartz boat 35 x 20 x 12 mm, 6 g, holding a 10 x 10 x 0.5 mm SiO2/Si chip face up. In line with the tube's near end, a stainless push rod, 500 mm long and 6 mm round with a 10 mm pusher disc, 110 g, lies on two V-topped rests.
scoring: 0 if any boat tips over 20 degrees or drops 30 mm, or the chip slides over 3 mm on its boat or tilts over 30 degrees, at any time; 0 unless the boats, chip and rod moved under 1 mm in the last second. Otherwise 0.25 for each boat in the tube on its floor and in place: sulfur centred within 15 mm of 10 mm inside the furnace's near (upstream) end; MoO3 centred within 10 mm of the thermocouple; the chip boat's centre 50 to 80 mm downstream of the MoO3 boat's. 1.0 if all three are in place, the rod is back within 15 mm of its start and every fingertip is 8 cm or more from the rod and the boats.
reset_notes: Put the boats back on the tray and the rod on its rests; the powders and the chip are reused.
fidelity: Rigid-body sim. Furnace, tube, tray and rests are fixed; boats, chip and rod are loose with real sizes and masses. Powder is a solid layer in each boat, so spills are scored by tilt. No heat, gas flow or growth: the layout is scored from positions. The tube's floor is a flat quartz strip as wide as a boat.
